Keys: 'note' (HTML, appended to the description), 'perm' (name of the Project Settings permission the row needs, see EngineApi.cpp perm::allowed), 'script_sig' / 'script_returns' (the Lua/Python call when it differs from the registry signature), 'examples' ({lua, python} source, rendered with the language switcher). examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- True when target lies within coneDeg degrees around the direction
-- (fx, fy, fz) this entity faces.
function M.canSee(self, target, fx, fy, fz, coneDeg)
    local x, y, z = horizon.getPosition(self.entityId)
    local tx, ty, tz = horizon.getPosition(target)
    local dx, dy, dz = horizon.math.normalize3(tx - x, ty - y, tz - z)
    local limit = horizon.math.cos(horizon.math.radians(coneDeg / 2))
    return horizon.math.dot3(dx, dy, dz, fx, fy, fz) >= limit
end

return M
examples.python:
import horizon

class ViewCone(horizon.Behavior):
    def can_see(self, target, fx, fy, fz, cone_deg):
        """True when target lies within cone_deg degrees around (fx, fy, fz)."""
        x, y, z = horizon.getPosition(self.entity_id)
        tx, ty, tz = horizon.getPosition(target)
        dx, dy, dz = horizon.math.normalize3(tx - x, ty - y, tz - z)
        limit = horizon.math.cos(horizon.math.radians(cone_deg / 2))
        return horizon.math.dot3(dx, dy, dz, fx, fy, fz) >= limit

local M = {}

-- "volume = 75" -> "volume", 75. Positions count from 0.
local function parse(line)
    local eq = horizon.string.find(line, "=")
    if eq < 0 then return nil end
    local key = horizon.string.trim(horizon.string.substring(line, 0, eq))
    local rest = horizon.string.substring(line, eq + 1, horizon.string.length(line))
    return key, horizon.string.toNumber(rest)
end

function M.onStart(self)
    local key, value = parse("volume = 75")
    if key then horizon.log(key .. " is " .. value) end
end

return M

local M = {}

function M.onStart(self)
    -- Without this, every launch rolls the same numbers. Seed in one
    -- script only: every seed restarts the sequence for all of them.
    horizon.random.seed(os.time())
end

function M.roll(self)
    local eyes = horizon.random.rangeInt(1, 6)      -- 1 to 6, both included

import horizon

class Dice(horizon.Behavior):
    def on_start(self):
        # Without this, every launch rolls the same numbers. Seed in one

time.pause.note: Input actions stop arriving unless they have Fires while the game is paused ticked.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- "Pause" is an input action with "Fires while the game is paused"
-- ticked; without it the second press would never arrive.
function M.onInputPressed(self, name)
    if name ~= "Pause" then return end
    if horizon.time.isPaused() then
        horizon.time.resume()
    else
        horizon.time.pause()
    end
end

function M.onCollisionEnter(self, other)
    horizon.time.hitStop(0.1)   -- a landed hit freezes for a tenth of a second
end

return M

examples.lua:
local M = {}
local LIMIT = 90   -- seconds for the level

-- This script sits on the HUD's UI Text entity.
function M.onStart(self)
    self.left = LIMIT
end

function M.onUpdate(self, dt)
    if self.left <= 0 then return end
    self.left = math.max(0, self.left - dt)
    local e = self.entityId
    horizon.ui.setText(e, string.format("%d:%02d", self.left // 60, math.floor(self.left) % 60))
    if self.left < 10 then
        horizon.ui.setColor(e, 1, 0.25, 0.2, 1)   -- a colour is four numbers
    end
    if self.left == 0 then
        horizon.ui.setVisible(e, false)
    end
end

return M

local M = {}
local MENU = "UI/pause_menu.hasset"   -- a widget with an element called "Panel"

function M.onStart(self)
    self.menu = horizon.createWidget(MENU)   -- starts hidden; 0 if the asset is missing
end

function M.onInputPressed(self, name)
    if name ~= "Pause" or self.paused or self.menu == 0 then return end
    self.paused = true
    horizon.time.pause()
    horizon.showCursor()
    -- A dialog: dims the game, takes the input, closes on Escape or Back.
    horizon.widget.showModal(self.menu)
    horizon.widget.animate(self.menu, "Panel", "Render Opacity", 0, 0, "Linear")
    horizon.widget.animate(self.menu, "Panel", "Render Opacity", 1, 0.2, "Out Quad")
end

function M.onUpdate(self, dt)
    -- A script gets no On Dismissed: notice the close by asking.
    if self.paused and not horizon.widget.isVisible(self.menu) then
        self.paused = false
        horizon.time.resume()
        horizon.hideCursor()
    end
end

return M

import horizon

MENU = "UI/pause_menu.hasset"   # a widget with an element called "Panel"

class PauseMenu(horizon.Behavior):
    paused = False

    def on_start(self):
        self.menu = horizon.createWidget(MENU)   # starts hidden; 0 if the asset is missing

    def on_input_pressed(self, name):
        if name != "Pause" or self.paused or self.menu == 0:
            return
        self.paused = True
        horizon.time.pause()
        horizon.showCursor()
        # A dialog: dims the game, takes the input, closes on Escape or Back.
        horizon.widget.showModal(self.menu)
        horizon.widget.animate(self.menu, "Panel", "Render Opacity", 0, 0, "Linear")
        horizon.widget.animate(self.menu, "Panel", "Render Opacity", 1, 0.2, "Out Quad")

    def on_update(self, dt):
        # A script gets no On Dismissed: notice the close by asking.
        if self.paused and not horizon.widget.isVisible(self.menu):
            self.paused = False
            horizon.time.resume()
            horizon.hideCursor()

local M = {}
local PLAYER = "Player 1"

function M.onStart(self)
    -- Lands in the project's Saved folder, but needs the "Files outside the
    -- project" permission all the same (see the group notes).
    self.db = horizon.db.open("scores.db")
    if self.db ~= 0 then
        horizon.db.exec(self.db, "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scores(name TEXT, points INTEGER)", "")
    end
end

function M.onInputPressed(self, name)
    if name ~= "LevelDone" or self.db == 0 then return end
    local points = math.max(0, 1000 - math.floor(horizon.time.elapsed() * 10))
    -- Values travel as a JSON array behind the ?s, never pasted into the SQL.
    -- json.set* can overwrite array slots but not add them, so start from two.
    local params = horizon.json.setNumber(horizon.json.setString('["", 0]', "[0]", PLAYER), "[1]", points)
    if not horizon.db.exec(self.db, "INSERT INTO scores(name, points) VALUES(?, ?)", params) then
        horizon.log("scores: " .. horizon.db.lastError(self.db))
        return
    end
    local rows = horizon.db.query(self.db,
        "SELECT name, points FROM scores ORDER BY points DESC LIMIT 5", "")
    for i = 0, horizon.json.count(rows, "") - 1 do
        horizon.log(string.format("%d. %s  %d", i + 1,
            horizon.json.getString(rows, "[" .. i .. "].name", "?"),
            horizon.json.getNumber(rows, "[" .. i .. "].points", 0)))
    end
end

return M

local M = {}
local URL = "https://example.com/news.json"   -- answers {"headline": "..."}

-- This script sits on a UI Text entity; the headline goes there.
function M.onStart(self)
    self.ticket = horizon.http.get(URL)   -- 0: no "Network access" permission
    horizon.ui.setText(self.entityId, self.ticket ~= 0 and "Loading..." or "")
end

function M.onUpdate(self, dt)
    local t = self.ticket
    -- A script gets no On Http Response: ask until the ticket is answered.
    if t == 0 or not horizon.http.done(t) then return end
    self.ticket = 0
    if not horizon.http.ok(t) then                    -- never reached the server
        horizon.ui.setText(self.entityId, "Offline")
        horizon.log("news: " .. horizon.http.error(t))
    elseif horizon.http.status(t) ~= 200 then         -- reached it, and it said no
        horizon.ui.setText(self.entityId, "")
        horizon.log("news: HTTP " .. horizon.http.status(t))
    else
        local body = horizon.http.body(t)
        horizon.ui.setText(self.entityId, horizon.json.getString(body, "headline", ""))
    end
    horizon.http.forget(t)
end

return M
examples.python:
import horizon

URL = "https://example.com/news.json"   # answers {"headline": "..."}

# This script sits on a UI Text entity; the headline goes there.
class FetchNews(horizon.Behavior):
    def on_start(self):
        self.ticket = horizon.http.get(URL)   # 0: no "Network access" permission
        horizon.ui.setText(self.entity_id, "Loading..." if self.ticket else "")

    def on_update(self, dt):
        t = self.ticket
        # A script gets no On Http Response: ask until the ticket is answered.
        if t == 0 or not horizon.http.done(t):
            return
        self.ticket = 0
        if not horizon.http.ok(t):                     # never reached the server
            horizon.ui.setText(self.entity_id, "Offline")
            horizon.log("news: " + horizon.http.error(t))
        elif horizon.http.status(t) != 200:            # reached it, and it said no
            horizon.ui.setText(self.entity_id, "")
            horizon.log("news: HTTP %d" % horizon.http.status(t))
        else:
            body = horizon.http.body(t)
            horizon.ui.setText(self.entity_id, horizon.json.getString(body, "headline", ""))
        horizon.http.forget(t)

local M = {}
local SLOT = "slot1"

-- "level" (Int) and "stats" (a struct with "kills") are fields of the
-- project's SaveGame Template.
function M.onStart(self)
    -- Continue from the save if there is one, else start a new one.
    if not (horizon.save.exists(SLOT) and horizon.save.load(SLOT)) then
        horizon.save.create(SLOT)
    end
    horizon.log(string.format("Level %d", horizon.save.getNumber("level", 1)))
end

-- This entity is the checkpoint's trigger volume.
function M.onBeginOverlap(self, other)
    horizon.save.setNumber("level", horizon.save.getNumber("level", 1) + 1)
    local stats = horizon.save.getStruct("stats")   -- keeps __type
    stats.kills = stats.kills + 1
    horizon.save.setStruct("stats", stats)
    horizon.save.write()   -- nothing is on disk before this
end

return M

import horizon

SLOT = "slot1"

class Checkpoint(horizon.Behavior):
    # "level" (Int) and "stats" (a struct with "kills") are fields of the
    # project's SaveGame Template.
    def on_start(self):
        # Continue from the save if there is one, else start a new one.
        if not (horizon.save.exists(SLOT) and horizon.save.load(SLOT)):
            horizon.save.create(SLOT)
        horizon.log(f"Level {horizon.save.getNumber('level', 1):.0f}")

    # This entity is the checkpoint's trigger volume.
    def on_begin_overlap(self, other):
        horizon.save.setNumber("level", horizon.save.getNumber("level", 1) + 1)
        stats = horizon.save.getStruct("stats")   # keeps __type
        stats["kills"] += 1
        horizon.save.setStruct("stats", stats)
        horizon.save.write()   # nothing is on disk before this

physics.raycast.script_returns: hit, entity, px, py, pz, nx, ny, nz, distance, layer
physics.raycast.note: A ray that starts inside a collider hits it at distance 0, so a ray from a character's own position finds the character. Sees trigger volumes.

examples.lua:
local M = {}
local REACH = 2.0   -- metres in front of the character
local PUSH  = 4.0   -- impulse, newton-seconds

-- "Interact" is a button action. Pushes whatever dynamic body is in front.
function M.onInputPressed(self, name)
    if name ~= "Interact" then return end
    local e = self.entityId
    local x, y, z = horizon.getPosition(e)
    local _, yaw = horizon.getRotation(e)
    local r = horizon.math.radians(yaw)
    local fx, fz = -horizon.math.sin(r), -horizon.math.cos(r)   -- facing, -Z at yaw 0
    -- Start a step ahead: a ray from inside the own capsule would hit it.
    local ox, oz = x + fx * 0.75, z + fz * 0.75
    local hit, other, px, py, pz = horizon.physics.raycast(ox, y, oz, fx, 0, fz, REACH)
    if hit and horizon.physics.hasPhysics(other) then
        -- The hit point is world space, which is what AtPosition expects.
        horizon.physics.addImpulseAtPosition(other, fx * PUSH, 0, fz * PUSH, px, py, pz)
    end
end

return M

import horizon

REACH = 2.0   # metres in front of the character
PUSH = 4.0    # impulse, newton-seconds

class PushCrate(horizon.Behavior):
    # "Interact" is a button action. Pushes whatever dynamic body is in front.
    def on_input_pressed(self, name):
        if name != "Interact":

        e = self.entity_id
        x, y, z = horizon.getPosition(e)
        _, yaw, _ = horizon.getRotation(e)
        r = horizon.math.radians(yaw)
        fx, fz = -horizon.math.sin(r), -horizon.math.cos(r)   # facing, -Z at yaw 0
        # Start a step ahead: a ray from inside the own capsule would hit it.
        ox, oz = x + fx * 0.75, z + fz * 0.75
        hit, other, px, py, pz, *_ = horizon.physics.raycast(ox, y, oz, fx, 0, fz, REACH)
        if hit and horizon.physics.hasPhysics(other):
            # The hit point is world space, which is what AtPosition expects.
            horizon.physics.addImpulseAtPosition(other, fx * PUSH, 0, fz * PUSH, px, py, pz)

examples.lua:
local M = {}
local FLOOR = -20   -- below this height the character has fallen out

function M.onStart(self)
    self.sx, self.sy, self.sz = horizon.getPosition(self.entityId)
end

function M.onUpdate(self, dt)
    local _, y = horizon.getPosition(self.entityId)
    if y < FLOOR then
        -- Back to where the level started it, without the speed of the fall.
        horizon.physics.setPositionAndReset(self.entityId, self.sx, self.sy, self.sz)
    end
end

return M

local M = {}

-- preset: W is +y), "Sprint" and "Jump" are button actions.

    local e = self.entityId

    -- default) that is away from the camera.

nav.moveTo.note: The point must lie on the NavMesh surface; the same x/z five metres above it is refused.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- On an entity with a Nav Agent. World positions on the baked NavMesh.
local POINTS = { {6, 0, -6}, {6, 0, 6}, {-6, 0, 6} }

local function goNext(self)
    self.i = self.i % #POINTS + 1
    local p = POINTS[self.i]
    if not horizon.nav.moveTo(self.entityId, p[1], p[2], p[3]) then
        horizon.log("patrol point " .. self.i .. " is not reachable")
    end
end

function M.onStart(self)
    self.i = 0
    goNext(self)
end

function M.onUpdate(self, dt)
    -- isMoving turns false on arrival (and after a refusal).
    if not horizon.nav.isMoving(self.entityId) then goNext(self) end
end

return M

-- The walk clip carries "FootL" and "FootR" notifies on its timeline.

    if name ~= "FootL" and name ~= "FootR" then return end

    self.step = horizon.audio.playAt(STEP, x, y, z, 0.7, pitch, false, 1, 25)
end

class Footsteps(horizon.Behavior):

examples.lua:
local M = {}
local MUSIC = "Audio/theme.hasset"
local VOLUME, FADE = 0.6, 2.0   -- fade length in seconds

function M.onStart(self)
    self.music = horizon.audio.play(MUSIC, VOLUME, 1, true)
    self.left = 0
end

-- "EndLevel" is a button action.
function M.onInputPressed(self, name)
    if name == "EndLevel" and self.music ~= 0 then self.left = FADE end
end

function M.onUpdate(self, dt)
    if self.left <= 0 then return end
    self.left = self.left - dt
    if self.left <= 0 then
        horizon.audio.stop(self.music)   -- stop, not volume 0: frees the voice
        self.music = 0
    else
        horizon.audio.setVolume(self.music, VOLUME * self.left / FADE)
    end
end

return M
